correctness.rationale: Substituting the published covariant transformation into the EAIE is exact: each step increment gains \(\zeta_{m,k}\), while the grand value gains every grade shift and the balancing subtraction removes only the top-grade shift for each factor. The surviving common defect is therefore \(|F|^{-1}\sum_j\sum_{q<d_j}\zeta_{j,q}\). The displayed \(d=(2,1)\) witness gives shifts \((3/2,1/2,1/2)\) instead of \((1,0,0)\). The inspected publisher PDF visibly makes the disputed replacement in the proof of Lemma 3.4 by retaining only the highest-grade shifts. Thus universal COTR holds exactly in the binary-grade case, and the theorem that characterizes the same rule using COTR cannot remain correct as written on a genuine multigrade domain.
residual_risks: The conclusion is limited to the printed EAIE/COTR characterization and does not invalidate unrelated dynamic results.
